head: 985ac9d92fdec48ddac395d7796d68ee0bdc8ea8
classification_reasons: Spec is not tight by the article's bar in the usual sense: it hits sdlc.yaml risk_list item 'auth' end to end (an authorization control), and the design's own Flagged concern 3 accepts a residual heuristic-parsing gap rather than closing it outright -- acceptance, not elimination, of that gap.

Blast radius is wide: shell_guard.py's decide() is new surface running on every Bash/PowerShell call in every phase, by hand and in CI; a second layer (sandbox.filesystem.denyWrite) is added to plugin/ci/settings.ci.json, template/.claude/settings.json and plugin/ci/run_phase.py's ci_settings_file, read by every CI phase job.

No existing test exercises a Bash/PowerShell write to a guardrail or locked test file today -- that bypass is exactly the intent's finding -- so the planned behavior is new, not already covered by current tests, even though the plan correctly orders reproducing-tests-first.
attempted: Intent: compared the current spec.md/plan.md against intent.md's proposed outcome (every instance of the authz-by-tool-route pattern fixed, each proven by a test, an eval case for the class). The design still finds the second instance (test_file_lock.py), still plans both eval cases under the corrected names, and adds the sandbox write-deny layer as a second control. No scope drift from intent in this round.

Spec and plan: read this round's actual change -- plan.md's 'Files that change' bullet that used to name both .claude-plugin/plugin.json and .claude-plugin/marketplace.json on one line is now two bullets, each naming exactly one path, which is what plan_sync.py's one-path-per-bullet parser needs to pick up both manifest bumps named in Order of work step 8. Checked every other bullet in 'Files that change' names exactly one path (it does: shell_guard.py, hooks.json, settings.ci.json, template/.claude/settings.json, run_phase.py, tests/test_hooks.py, tests/test_ci.py, the two eval-case folders, framework-evals.yml, OPERATING_MODEL.md, each its own bullet). Confirmed the three Flagged concerns in spec.md each still open with the word 'decided' and name what the decision rests on; confirmed the eval-case proof command is plugin/evals/run.py everywhere in both spec.md and plan.md (the prior round's evals/check.py defect is gone, in both the Acceptance section and Order of work step 9 / Proof).

Proof: phase (b) produces no toolchain logs by design (plan.md states tests are still to be written in phase (c)); evidence/ contains only the run/evidence/decision records appropriate to a design-only phase, consistent with that. Cross-checked status.yaml's risk_accepted/risk_accepted_by state against plugin/state/status.py and plugin/gate/checks.py's check_owner_actions and decision 24: risk_accepted now carries 'auth' with risk_accepted_by empty, which plugin/state/status.py documents as the expected shape for the by-hand CLI route (a commit by the owner's own identity is the act; risk_accepted_by is populated only for the label route) -- matches the owner's own round-2 review comment ('do not write risk_accepted or risk_accepted_by ... by-hand route'). The stale gate/parked_reason block left in status.yaml from the earlier park is a record of a prior run, not a claim about this diff's correctness, and will be overwritten by the next deterministic gate run.

Blast radius: confirmed the diff for this round touches only changes/0002.../{plan.md, spec.md, status.yaml, evidence/**} -- no source file -- matching phase (b) being a read-only/design-only run (CLAUDE.md: 'the plan.md run is read-only'). Confirmed sdlc.yaml risk_list's 'auth' is the only item implicated; no data-migration, money-movement or production-config path touched by the design.

Policies: security-baseline rule 1 (authorization not inferred from tool route) is the requirement itself, correctly sourced; rule 6 (no new dependency) is honored; decision 24's label-vs-by-hand risk-acceptance mechanics (checked directly against plugin/state/status.py and plugin/gate/checks.py) are followed correctly for this round's status.yaml state. coding-standards rule 2 (reuse) and rule 4 (no weakening existing tests) are both addressed in Requirements/Acceptance; nothing in this round's diff touches a guardrail file (.claude/**, CLAUDE.md, REVIEW.md, sdlc.yaml).

Tests: no test code exists yet (phase (b) is design-only); re-checked that the planned test shape (reproducing tests first, direct unit tests of shell_write_targets and its negative list, wiring and ci_settings_file tests, two --dry-run-validated eval cases) still matches intent's 'test first' constraint and would actually exercise the bypass rather than merely assert the plan's wording. This round's only change (the bullet split) does not touch any test file or test plan.
